item.title: UE rejeita totalmente qualquer proibição sobre diesel, diz porta-voz da UE
item.description: A União Europeia “rejeita totalmente” a ameaça feita pelos EUA de proibir as exportações de diesel caso a Europa não libere uma quantidade maior de seus estoques de combustível, afirmou na sexta-feira a porta-voz da Comissão Europeia Anna-Kaisa Itkonen.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A União Europeia “rejeita totalmente” a ameaça feita pelos EUA de proibir as exportações de diesel caso a Europa não libere uma quantidade maior de seus estoques de combustível, afirmou na sexta-feira a porta-voz da Comissão Europeia Anna-Kaisa Itkonen. “Uma proibição não seria benéfica para ninguém. Isso minaria nossa confiança nos Estados Unidos como um parceiro confiável”, disse ela, acrescentando que a próxima reunião do Grupo de Coordenação do Petróleo da UE está marcada para 15 de outubro, mas pode ser antecipada se necessário.

item.content:encoded: Looking for inspiration? Every Friday, Weekend Reads rounds up what the Reuters Open Interest team has been reading, watching and listening to. This week's picks explore AI's trillion-dollar ambitions, the financial fallout of geopolitical risk and the global race for critical minerals — plus much more. This weekend, we're reading... ANNA SZYMANSKI, ROI Editor-in-Charge: Anthropic's IPO prospectus made waves this week following a Reuters exclusive. In a series of stories, Reuters broke down the key details, from the company's AI vision and its [USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"half-a-trillion-dollar spending plan"] to further warnings of [USN:L4N45K1J5 TEXT:""existential risks to humanity""] posed by advanced AI. MIKE DOLAN, ROI Finance & Markets Columnist: In this CEPR VoxEU column, Bank of England researchers explain how banks systematically curtail lending to firms exposed to geopolitical risk. While the effects of geopolitics on trade and investment flows are well documented, the impact on credit channels is less well known. ANDY HOME, ROI Metals Columnist: This immersive report from the World Bank Group breaks down the potential economic and social benefits arising from responsible mining in countries such as Zambia and Chile, both production powerhouses for critical metals such as copper and lithium. We're listening to... And we're watching... ANNA SZYMANSKI, ROI Editor-in-Charge: How profoundly could AI reshape the jobs market? This is one of the biggest questions facing workers, employers, policymakers, and investors today. But if the outlook is uncertain for the current generation of workers, what about the next? In the latest episode of The Big View , Peter Thal Larsen, global editor of Reuters Breakingviews, sits down with academic and author Daniel Susskind to talk about what can be done to prepare future workers for a world of AI. item.title: Cobre sube por debilidad del dólar, pero inversores se muestran cautos sobre demanda
item.description: Los precios del cobre subían el viernes, impulsados por la debilidad del dólar y los problemas de suministro, pero las alzas son moderadas debido a la preocupación por la posibilidad de que los elevados precios del petróleo afecten a la demanda.
item.dc:creator: Eric Onstad
item.content:encoded: Los precios del cobre subían el viernes, impulsados por la debilidad del dólar y los problemas de suministro, pero las alzas son moderadas debido a la preocupación por la posibilidad de que los elevados precios del petróleo afecten a la demanda. * A las 1000 GMT, el contrato de referencia del cobre a tres meses en la Bolsa de Metales de Londres (LME) ganaba un 0,3%, a 14.289 dólares por tonelada, pero acumula un descenso del 2% en la semana. * "Los metales han vuelto a registrar un volumen de negociación reducido en la sesión y el cobre ha encontrado cierto apoyo gracias a un dólar algo más débil, pero el tono general sigue siendo de cautela", señaló en una nota Neil Welsh, de la correduría Britannia Global Markets. * "Los elevados costos energéticos derivados del actual conflicto entre Estados Unidos e Irán y los indicios de debilidad industrial en China han lastrado la confianza en todo el sector", agregó. * El índice dólar alcanzó esta semana su nivel más alto en 17 meses, pero se debilitaba el viernes, abaratando las materias primas cotizadas en la divisa estadounidense para los compradores con otras monedas. * El cobre en la LME ha subido un 16% en los últimos seis meses, debido en gran parte a un importante desplazamiento de las existencias hacia Estados Unidos, atraídas por la perspectiva de posibles aranceles en ese país, lo que ha provocado escasez en otros lugares. * Las existencias en los almacenes supervisados por la Bolsa de Futuros de Shangái se han desplomado un 79% en los últimos cuatro meses, a 38.744 toneladas, su nivel más bajo desde enero de 2024. La SHFE permanece cerrada con motivo de la Fiesta Nacional de China y volverá a abrir el 8 de octubre. * En otros metales básicos, el aluminio en la LME subía un 0,5%, a 3.137 dólares la tonelada; el zinc ganaba un 0,1%, a 3.729 dólares; el plomo sumaba un 0,4%, a 1.864 dólares; el níquel avanzaba un 0,3%, a 15.675 dólares; y el estaño mejoraba un 0,3%, a 54.500 dólares.

item.title: Morning Bid: Yield to worst
item.description: The third quarter of 2026 won't be forgotten soon – even if bond investors might prefer to.
item.dc:creator: Anna Szymanski
item.content:encoded: The third quarter of 2026 won't be forgotten soon – even if bond investors might prefer to. The last three months have seen government bond yields hit multi-decade highs, diesel prices reach all-time peaks and crude prices rise back above $100 a barrel as the Middle East conflict passed the seven-month mark. And lest we forget, investors also learned of threats to the future of humanity itself amid news of rogue AI agents and [USN:L6N45E0VV TEXT:"dire warnings"] from tech leaders. Yet global equities continued to [USN:L8N45G0H5 TEXT:"grind higher"] in the period, fuelled by eye-popping corporate earnings growth, setting up a further [USN:L6N45N036 TEXT:"test of resilience"] in the fourth quarter. The [USN:L8N45N0KW TEXT:"bond market"] hogged much of the spotlight again this week. The benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield [USN:L1N45N05N TEXT:"hit a 24-year high"] of 5.34% on Thursday, after rising more than 80 basis points in the third quarter. While a [USN:L6N45M1FL TEXT:"sharp rally"] on Thursday pushed down yields, it's still far too early to breathe a sigh of relief. The pain during the week was also felt in European bond markets, particularly in France, where yields hit a 24-year high on Thursday, nearing the psychologically important 5% level, having recorded a jump of around 120 basis points in the third quarter. Fiscal concerns in the euro zone's second-largest economy helped blow out the spread between French and German sovereign bond yields to more than 140 basis points, the widest since 2012. This [USN:L6N45N0DC TEXT:"jarred"] European stocks and [USN:L1N45N00X TEXT:"hit the euro"]. In Japan, the 10-year government bond yield rose on Friday, nearing the 30-year high of 3.115% reached last week, after investors learned that inflation in Tokyo rose in September at the [USN:L4N45M0C3 TEXT:"fastest pace in 10 months"]. Markets are betting the Bank of Japan will increase interest rates again in December. Speaking of rate hikes, Australia's central bank was the latest to [USN:P8N3X1041 TEXT:"lift its policy rate"] on Tuesday, voting unanimously to increase it by 25 basis points to 4.60%, a 15-year high, with the market expecting more hikes to come. Yet the week also brought one sign that the bond rout may be slightly overdone. The 2-year US Treasury yield edged lower midweek after New York Federal Reserve President John Williams on Tuesday said there was "[USN:S0N44U01W TEXT:"no need for urgency""] regarding another Fed rate hike in October. The implied probability of an October rate rise subsequently tumbled from around 70% to below 50%. Williams' comments came amid the release of several relatively soft economic data points, including a drop in August [USN:L1N45K0MO TEXT:"job openings"], dismal September [USN:AQN2MLCVJ TEXT:"consumer confidence"] numbers and, on Wednesday, a [USN:L1N45L0SG TEXT:"lower-than-expected"] 3.4% August annual inflation print from the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, the Fed's preferred gauge. Still, inflation remains well above the central bank's 2% target, and economic growth and corporate earnings both remain robust, suggesting that bonds may get [USN:L6N45K107 TEXT:"squeezed even more"] in the coming months. Shifting to politics, UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham gave a relatively [USN:L8N45K1LP TEXT:"bold speech"] at the Labour Party conference on Tuesday as he pledged to revive Britain's economy by tackling social care, housing and utilities and also hinted that a return to the European Union was not out of the question. While undoing Brexit seems unlikely, even the hint of it has the [USN:L6N45M17D TEXT:"potential to boost sterling assets"]. Moving further east, the conflict between the US and Iran may be heating up yet again. Washington is sending additional warships and troops to the region, according to a Wall Street Journal report, raising expectations that large-scale military strikes could resume after the US midterm elections in November. Tehran is preparing a broad and forceful response, [USN:L8N45M1N4 TEXT:"according to Reuters sources"], while continuing a diplomatic push that Iranian officials have privately indicated is unlikely to succeed. Brent crude [USN:L1N45N00Y TEXT:"settled up"] more than 4% on Thursday, but prices were [USN:L4N45O016 TEXT:"down slightly"] early on Friday, as investors weighed elevated geopolitical risk with news that more oil is exiting the Gulf. Diesel remains the real pain point, particularly following news that Chinese refiners were [USN:L4N45N0A8 TEXT:"suspending"] October fuel exports. The Trump administration is pressuring France and Germany to release diesel from their emergency inventories or potentially face a [USN:L6N45N0FO TEXT:"US diesel export ban"]. European Union countries on Friday [USN:B5N44301Y TEXT:"discussed"] a French proposal to release additional stockpiles in response, according to Reuters sources. All is a bit quieter on the trade war front. China and the US [USN:P8N42O09S TEXT:"announced"] early in the week that they would pursue tariff cuts on $60 billion worth of goods imported from each other, ranging from US corn to Chinese toys. Over in tech, Reuters had an exclusive look at the Anthropic IPO prospectus, [USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"which showed that"] the AI giant – which is aiming for a $2 trillion valuation – saw its revenue surge 12-fold in 2025 to nearly $4.6 billion, while operating losses more than doubled to over $8 billion. The prospectus also highlighted [USN:L6N45K15A TEXT:"how dependent"] the young firm is on a small group of customers. And the document included a [USN:L4N45K1J5 TEXT:"warning"] not commonly found in such filings: "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity." Good luck pricing that. Staying in tech, Nvidia boosted its share buyback authorization by a [USN:L6N45K0LY TEXT:"record $150 billion"], eclipsing Apple's $110 billion approval in 2024. Finally, all eyes will be on the September US nonfarm payrolls data due later today. Consensus forecasts are for a gain of [USN:L1N45N0X3 TEXT:"90,000 jobs"] and a steady unemployment rate of 4.1%. Next week will be light on economic releases, but investors will get more insight into the Fed's thinking with the release of the minutes from last month's FOMC meeting. Happy reading! Before you head off, take a look at some questions ROI columnists have recently been exploring: Why can't the US grow its [USN:L6N45H0VH TEXT:"way out of its debt woes?"] What multi-trillion spending trend could reshape the global economy? [USN:L6N45L0QW TEXT:"(Hint: it's not AI.)"] Why isn't inflation data as [USN:L1N45L0IP TEXT:"straightforward as it seems?"] How is the energy transition [USN:L1N45H0UI TEXT:"beginning to feed itself?"] What warning sign is Bangladesh [USN:L1N45L0WX TEXT:"sending to the LNG market?"] What will cash-rich oil majors' strategy [USN:L6N45H0N6 TEXT:"look like after the Iran war?"] Which Asian equity markets and sectors are [USN:L1N45E010 TEXT:"most vulnerable to Fed tightening?"] Will the drop in global demand for seaborne coal [USN:L4N45L0NN TEXT:"offset the decline in supply?"] Are AI credit tremors a [USN:L6N45K13P TEXT:"warning or a "buy" signal?"] How exactly do you [USN:L8N45N16J TEXT:"price alumina?"] I'd love to hear from you, so please reach out to me at anna.szymanski@thomsonreuters.com Want to receive the Morning Bid in your inbox every weekday morning? item.content:encoded: Schwedens Wahlsiegerin Magdalena Andersson soll im Ringen um eine Regierungsbildung einen zweiten Anlauf starten. Die Chefin der Sozialdemokraten wurde am Freitag erneut damit betraut, obwohl sie am Montag eine Regierungsbildung wegen fehlenden Rückhalts für unmöglich erklärt hatte. Bei der Wahl am 13. September hatte Anderssons Mitte-Links-Lager zwar knapp gewonnen. Die vier Parteien ihres Blocks sind sich jedoch uneins darüber, wer an einer neuen Regierung beteiligt werden soll. Deshalb hatte Andersson die Regierungsbildung zunächst aufgegeben. Parlamentspräsident Andreas Norlen verwies bei seinem neuen Auftrag auf die Sitzverteilung zugunsten Anderssons. Ihre Allianz stellt nach der Wahl 176 Abgeordnete, während das rechte Bündnis des amtierenden Ministerpräsidenten Ulf Kristersson nur auf 173 Mandate kommt. Parlamentspräsident Norlen erklärte, die politischen und parlamentarischen Bedingungen seien unverändert. Daher sei es vernünftig, dass Andersson ihre Sondierungsgespräche wieder aufnehme. Die 59-Jährige, die schon einmal Ministerpräsidentin war, muss Norlen nun bis zum 12. Oktober Bericht erstatten. Andersson hatte zunächst aufgegeben, nachdem die Linkspartei einen Kandidaten der konservativen Moderaten Sammlungspartei von Kristersson für das Amt des Parlamentspräsidenten unterstützt hatte. Dies habe ihre Bemühungen untergraben, eine Mitte-Links-Regierung zu bilden, sagte Andersson. Sie nehme die Botschaft der Linkspartei ernst. Deswegen und aufgrund ihrer ersten Sondierungsgespräche komme sie zu dem Schluss, dass ihr die Möglichkeit für die Bildung einer Regierung fehle, so Andersson am Montag. Als Anwärter für eine Regierungsbildung galt nach dem ersten gescheiterten Anlauf auch Kristersson. Bislang gibt es jedoch kaum Anzeichen dafür, dass der amtierende Ministerpräsident auf weniger Hindernisse stoßen würde. Schließlich müsste er die Unterstützung mindestens einer Mitte-Links-Partei gewinnen und gleichzeitig den Rückhalt der rechtspopulistischen Schwedendemokraten behalten.

item.content:encoded: Der seit Jahren kriselnde Warenhauskonzern Galeria rutscht zum vierten Mal binnen sechs Jahren in die Pleite. Ein Antrag auf Eröffnung eines Insolvenzverfahrens sei beim Amtsgericht Düsseldorf gestellt worden. "Der Antrag schafft den rechtlichen Rahmen, um die aktuelle Situation zu ordnen, das Unternehmen zu stabilisieren und die Voraussetzungen für eine nachhaltige Zukunft von Galeria zu schaffen", teilte Galeria am Freitag mit. Zu Details äußerte sich Galeria nicht. Der mit Umsatzrückgängen kämpfende Warenhauskonzern hatte sich zuletzt im Juni eine neue Kreditlinie bei einem auf Restrukturierungen spezialisierten US-Investor gesichert - doch diese reicht offenbar nicht aus. Nun müssen die noch rund 12.000 Beschäftigten erneut um ihre Zukunft fürchten. "Haarsträubende Managementfehler haben zu dieser Entwicklung geführt", kritisierte die Gewerkschaft Verdi. "Ich bedauere, dass die Umstrukturierungsmaßnahmen bei Galeria nicht schnell genug Erfolg gezeigt haben", sagte dagegen Galeria-Miteigentümer Bernd Beetz. "Die Mitarbeiter haben bis zum Ende an die Rettung geglaubt und hätten sie verdient", betonte der frühere Vorstandschef des Kosmetikkonzerns Coty. Galeria verfügt nach eigenen Angaben noch über 83 Filialen in 70 Städten. Der Düsseldorfer Konzern blickt auf eine turbulente Vergangenheit zurück. Unter anderem gehörte er früher zur in die Pleite geschlitterten Signa-Gruppe des jüngst wegen Insolvenzbetrugs verurteilten Tiroler Investors Rene Benko. Galeria war bereits in der Vergangenheit mehrfach in die Insolvenz gerutscht. Ein US-Investor und Beetz hatten die Kette vor rund zwei Jahren übernommen und hatten sich an ihrer Sanierung versucht. Doch rund lief es für Galeria nicht: Erst im Juli hatte der Konzern 33 Warenhäuser zur Disposition gestellt. Für diese Häuser führe das Management Gespräche über Mietkonditionen und Anpassungen der Verkaufsflächen. Seien diese nicht erfolgreich, stünden die Filialen vor dem Aus. Galeria leidet unter der Konkurrenz durch Online-Händler wie Amazon (AMZN.O) oder Zalando (ZALG.DE) . Auch Modeketten wie Zara oder H&M setzen dem Warenhauskonzern zu. Steigende Energiepreise dämpfen zudem die Kauflaune der Verbraucher. Einige Handelsexperten halten das Konzept Warenhaus mit großen Verkaufsflächen und breit gemischten Sortimenten insgesamt für überholt. Die erneute Krise kommt für Galeria zur Unzeit: Die Kette steuert auf das wichtige Weihnachtsgeschäft zu. Verdi-Vorstandsmitglied Silke Zimmer kritisierte, dass Galeria keine Erklärung zu den Umständen des Antrags geliefert habe. "Das bedeutet eine völlige Ungewissenheit für die 12.000 Kolleginnen und Kollegen in den 83 verbliebenen Filialen!" Die Beschäftigten bräuchten nun rasch einen Plan für die Zukunft.

item.title: El ganador de las elecciones en Brasil podría reformar sus instituciones ante aumento de puestos vacantes
item.description: El próximo presidente de Brasil heredará un número inusualmente elevado de puestos por cubrir en las instituciones más poderosas del país, con vacantes acumuladas en el Supremo Tribunal Federal, el banco central y los organismos reguladores económicos.
item.dc:creator: Marcela Ayres, Ricardo Brito
item.content:encoded: El próximo presidente de Brasil heredará un número inusualmente elevado de puestos por cubrir en las instituciones más poderosas del país, con vacantes acumuladas en el Supremo Tribunal Federal, el banco central y los organismos reguladores económicos. La creciente acumulación de puestos sin cubrir significa que el ganador de la reñida contienda entre el presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva y el senador Flávio Bolsonaro podría adquirir una influencia significativa sobre los organismos que ayudan a definir la política monetaria, supervisan los mercados financieros e interpretan la Constitución. Los dos candidatos se enfrentarán en la primera vuelta de las elecciones el domingo, y se prevé que lo más probable sea que haya una segunda vuelta a finales de mes. Las vacantes reflejan un cambio más amplio en la política brasileña: un Congreso cada vez más poderoso está utilizando la confirmación de los candidatos como herramienta de presión política, lo que merma el margen de maniobra del poder ejecutivo. Un Congreso predominantemente de derecha ha hecho valer este poder creciente durante el actual mandato de Lula retrasando la confirmación de varios de sus candidatos. Lula tampoco ha logrado presentar algunas candidaturas. Si bien antes las candidaturas se remitían rápidamente a las comisiones del Senado para su aprobación, muchos procesos de nominación se estancaron durante la pandemia, a la espera de la aprobación del presidente del Senado. El presidente del Senado, Davi Alcolumbre, ha mantenido esa práctica, concentrando el poder en el Senado y convirtiendo lo que antes era un trámite rutinario en una decisión política, dijo una persona familiarizada con el proceso, que pidió permanecer en el anonimato. El Palacio Presidencial y la oficina de Alcolumbre no respondieron a las solicitudes de comentarios. El uso de los nombramientos presidenciales como arma política ha hecho que el Ejecutivo se muestre reacio a presentar candidatos sin evaluar primero sus perspectivas en el Senado, dijo Rubens Beçak, profesor de Derecho de la Universidad de São Paulo. PUESTOS EN EL BANCO CENTRAL En el Banco Central, dos puestos del directorio —incluido el de política económica, que supervisa las previsiones antes de las decisiones sobre las tasas de interés— llevan vacíos desde enero, lo que supone un período récord de vacante para esos cargos. Lula aún no ha presentado candidatos. En abril, los senadores rechazaron al candidato de Lula para el Supremo Tribunal Federal, el fiscal general Jorge Messias, en un revés histórico que prolongó una vacante que ya lleva casi un año, la más larga desde el retorno de Brasil a la democracia en la década de 1980. La Comisión de Valores Mobiliarios (CVM) tiene vacantes en su consejo de administración desde finales de 2024, mientras que el organismo de defensa de la competencia (Cade), que carece de presidente y de dos miembros de su consejo, se encuentra cerca de su quórum mínimo, lo que retrasa la tramitación de las fusiones. Claudio Couto, politólogo de la Fundación Getúlio Vargas, calificó este retraso de "profundamente problemático" y señaló que se corre el riesgo de concentrar los nombramientos en una sola administración y de politizar "órganos que deben permanecer apartidistas". CAMBIO ESTRUCTURAL Los nombramientos y los proyectos de ley, que antes se negociaban en gran medida entre el presidente y los partidos de la coalición, dependen cada vez más de acuerdos entre los líderes del Congreso, señaló Neuriberg Dias, director del observatorio legislativo DIAP. El creciente control del Congreso sobre el gasto, señaló, ha modificado los incentivos que subyacen a la negociación entre el poder ejecutivo y el legislativo. Las asignaciones presupuestarias del Congreso —que destinan fondos a proyectos locales o favoritos— representaron el 7,5% del gasto discrecional federal efectivo en 2018, pero aumentaron hasta el 21% en 2025, según datos del Ministerio de Planificación facilitados a Reuters. A su vez, el control del Gobierno sobre la agenda se ha debilitado. El año pasado, el Congreso aprobó 178 proyectos de ley presentados por los legisladores y solo 50 del Ejecutivo. En 2007, durante el segundo mandato de Lula, ocurrió lo contrario: 142 proyectos del Ejecutivo frente a 52 del Congreso, según datos de la DIAP. La campaña de 2026 ha ralentizado aún más las candidaturas, dijeron fuentes familiarizadas con el asunto, ya que los legisladores esperan a ver si Lula consigue otro mandato. Los votantes también elegirán a los 513 miembros de la Cámara de Diputados y a dos tercios del Senado. Con el poder desplazándose de la presidencia al Congreso, las elecciones podrían decidir no solo quién gobierna Brasil, sino también cuánto margen tendrá el ganador para nombrar cargos públicos y configurar instituciones clave.

item.title: Japão não precisa de política monetária excessivamente frouxa, diz ministro da Economia
item.description: O Japão não está mais passando por deflação e, portanto, não precisa de uma política monetária excessivamente frouxa para buscar uma taxa de inflação mais alta, afirmou nesta sexta-feira o ministro da Economia, Minoru Kiuchi.

item.content:encoded: O Japão não está mais passando por deflação e, portanto, não precisa de uma política monetária excessivamente frouxa para buscar uma taxa de inflação mais alta, afirmou nesta sexta-feira o ministro da Economia, Minoru Kiuchi. As decisões de política monetária são de competência do Banco do Japão, acrescentou Kiuchi, recusando-se a comentar se o governo se opõe a novos aumentos da taxa de juros pelo banco central. “O Japão saiu de uma era em que precisava do tipo de políticas reflacionistas adotadas no âmbito do Abenomics”, disse Kiuchi em uma coletiva de imprensa de rotina, acrescentando que as políticas da primeira-ministra Sanae Takaichi são diferentes do enorme pacote de estímulo introduzido pelo ex-primeiro-ministro Shinzo Abe em 2013. “O que quero dizer é que o Japão não está mais em um período deflacionário e, portanto, não precisa de uma política excessivamente frouxa que busque a inflação”, afirmou Kiuchi. Kiuchi fez essas declarações em resposta a perguntas de repórteres sobre um resumo das opiniões da reunião de política monetária do Banco do Japão realizada em setembro, que revelou que um representante do governo pediu cautela em relação a novos aumentos na taxa de juros. As declarações reforçam os comentários do governo que rejeitam a visão de que estaria adotando políticas reflacionistas para impulsionar a demanda por meio de medidas fiscais e monetárias expansionistas. A ministra da Fazenda, Satsuki Katayama, disse na terça-feira que deixou claro ao secretário do Tesouro dos EUA, Scott Bessent, na semana passada, que a primeira-ministra não é reflacionista. Kiuchi é amplamente considerado um reflacionista devido à sua cautela no passado em relação aos aumentos da taxa de juros e à sua associação com um grupo de parlamentares que defendia gastos expansionistas.

item.title: Futures in rialzo, calano rendimenti e greggio in attesa dati occupazione
item.description: I futures sugli indici azionari statunitensi sono in rialzo, a causa del calo dei rendimenti dei titoli del Tesoro legato alle minori probabilità di un aumento dei tassi d’interesse questo mese e della flessione dei prezzi del petrolio, mentre gli investitori attendono un importante rapporto sull’occupazione previsto nel corso della giornata.

item.content:encoded: I futures sugli indici azionari statunitensi sono in rialzo, a causa del calo dei rendimenti dei titoli del Tesoro legato alle minori probabilità di un aumento dei tassi d’interesse questo mese e della flessione dei prezzi del petrolio, mentre gli investitori attendono un importante rapporto sull’occupazione previsto nel corso della giornata. ** I prezzi del greggio Brent sono scesi sotto i 100 dollari al barile dopo indiscrezioni secondo cui l’Unione Europea ha discusso ulteriori rilasci di scorte di gasolio e greggio, anche se non ci sono stati nuovi aggiornamenti sulla risoluzione del conflitto in Medio Oriente. ** Sugli scudi i titoli dei chip e le megacap. NVIDIA (NVDA.O) guadagna quasi lo 0,9%, mentre BROADCOM (AVGO.O) e ADVANCED MICRO DEVICES (AMD.O) salgono di circa l’1% ciascuna. ALPHABET (GOOGL.O) e TESLA (TSLA.O) registrano un rialzo di quasi l’1% ciascuna. ** NIKE (NKE.N) perde il 10% dopo che l’azienda statunitense di abbigliamento sportivo ha previsto a sorpresa un drastico calo dei ricavi annuali a causa della debolezza del mercato cinese, ha annunciato tagli ai posti di lavoro e ha deciso di riorganizzare le proprie divisioni aziendali globali. ** L’attenzione degli investitori si sposterà sui dati sugli occupati non agricoli di settembre alle ore 14.30 italiane, con gli economisti che prevedono un rallentamento della crescita dell’occupazione negli Stati Uniti e il mantenimento della disoccupazione al 4,1% per il terzo mese consecutivo. ** Alle ore 12.05 italiane, i futures E-mini sul Dow sono in rialzo di 259 punti, pari allo 0,5%, mentre i futures E-mini sull’S&P 500 sono in rialzo di 36,25 punti, pari allo 0,5%. I futures E-mini sul Nasdaq 100 sono in rialzo di 246,25 punti, pari allo 0,8%. ** Il rendimento del titolo del Tesoro a 2 anni , più sensibile alle aspettative sui tassi, si mantiene vicino al minimo di oltre una settimana toccato ieri, quando gli investitori hanno segnalato un miglioramento del profilo rischio/rendimento a seguito della recente ondata di vendite. ** Secondo FedWatch Tool di CME Group, gli operatori ritengono che vi sia una probabilità del 76% che i tassi della Fed rimangano invariati a ottobre, in aumento rispetto al 29% circa di una settimana fa. ** Nonostante i rialzi della giornata, i principali indici di Wall Street si avviano a chiudere la settimana in ribasso, con l’S&P 500 (.SPX) che si dirige verso un calo dell’1%.

item.title: EU fully rejects any ban on diesel, EU spokesperson says
item.description: The European Union "fully rejects" the threat made by the U.S. to ban diesel exports if Europe does not release more of its fuel stocks, European Commission spokesperson Anna-Kaisa Itkonen said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The European Union "fully rejects" the threat made by the U.S. to ban [USN:L6N45O0G5 TEXT:"diesel exports"] if Europe does not release more of its fuel stocks, European Commission spokesperson Anna-Kaisa Itkonen said on Friday. "A ban would not be beneficial to anyone. It would undermine our trust in the United States as a reliable partner," she said, adding that the next EU's Oil Coordination Group meeting is scheduled on Oct. 15, but could be brought forward if needed.

item.title: Ally of Spanish PM threatens to derail housing decree as fury over evictions grows
item.description: Spain's leftist government faced a bruising battle in parliament on Friday after an allied party opposed its plans to tackle a housing crisis stirring public protests, particularly over the eviction of an 87-year-old woman.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Spain's leftist government faced a bruising battle in parliament on Friday after an allied party opposed its plans to tackle a housing crisis stirring [USN:L1N45K09H TEXT:"public protests"], particularly over the [USN:L8N45F0PQ TEXT:"eviction of an 87-year-old woman"]. Junts, a Catalan region separatist centre-right party with seven lawmakers, argued that the proposals would exacerbate matters by reducing housing supply. They include a ban on evictions of vulnerable tenants until 2030, a two-year rent freeze extension for existing leases, and tighter rules for short-term rentals. "Many of the measures included will produce the opposite effect of what is intended: they will reduce the supply of rental housing, drive up prices, and make it even harder for people with limited financial means to access housing," Junts said in a statement. The eviction of pensioner Maricarmen Abascal last week triggered protests across Spain, with many young people pitching tents in Madrid's central square and other cities for almost a week, bringing back memories of anti-austerity sit-ins sparked by the global financial crisis in 2008-12. Abascal's eviction unleashed anger over the cost of housing, with many young people living with parents past 30 years of age. SOARING RENTS Rents have doubled over the last decade with average prices reaching €1,176 ($1,323) a month, equivalent to 98.7% of the average salary for a young person, according to the Youth Council of Spain. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez's minority left-wing coalition government has 147 seats in the 350-seat chamber and relies on smaller parties, including Junts, to pass legislation. Opposition parties also oppose the decree. A second decree, which would permit automatic and indefinite renewal of rental contracts and was one of the protesters' main demands, was already expected not to pass because it had not secured the minimum support required. Elections are due next year, but Spanish media said Sanchez might call a snap vote if the main housing decree is not passed during Friday's session. Yolanda Diaz, a deputy prime minister and founder of the far-left flank of the ruling coalition, condemned opposition parties and Junts for threatening the decree. "Let them show their true colours; let the public know how each of them votes and what they want for the country," she told reporters. ($1 = 0.8890 euros)

item.title: Rogers completes full takeover of Leafs', Raptors' parent company
item.description: Rogers Communications Inc., already a 75% owner in Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment, bought the last 25% of the company on Thursday, paying Kilmer Sports Inc. $4.35 billion (Canadian).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Rogers Communications Inc., already a 75% owner in Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment, bought the last 25% of the company on Thursday, paying Kilmer Sports Inc. $4.35 billion (Canadian). MLSE owns the NBA's Toronto Raptors, the NHL's Toronto Maple Leafs, MLS' Toronto FC and the CFL's Toronto Argonauts in addition to Scotiabank Arena, home of the Raptors and Leafs. Rogers, whose media holdings include Sportsnet, also owns the Toronto Blue Jays and their home field, Rogers Centre. The company wrote in a press release, "Rogers will create a new business unit, Rogers Sports, that brings Rogers sports, media and entertainment businesses together including MLSE and the Toronto Blue Jays. "Now that we have completed the acquisition, Rogers will now build the best operating model for Rogers Sports." Rogers CEO Tony Staffieri added in a statement, "Our full ownership of MLSE brings together Canada's premier communications company with Canada's premier sports and entertainment organization. "It gives us even more opportunity to invest in championship-calibre teams, create unique experiences for customers and fans, and unlock long-term value for shareholders." Keith Pelley will stay on as MLSE's president and CEO, in addition to heading Rogers' media holdings. Mark Shapiro still will be the Blue Jays' president and CEO. Kilmer, the holding company of Canadian billionaire Larry Tanenbaum, reached the deal with Rogers regarding its share in MLSE in July. According to The Athletic, the agreement regarding the Maple Leafs and Raptors had to get approval from the teams' leagues to close by the end of the year. Rogers gained controlling interest in MLSE when it purchased 37.5% of the company from telecommunications firm Bell in a deal announced in September 2024. Within nine months, Rogers ousted the team presidents of the Maple Leafs and the Raptors. --Field Level Media

item.title: A través de la cocina, refugiados de Gaza forjan nueva vida en México
item.description: Los ruidos fuertes aún le generan ansiedad a Mohammed Abed, un ingeniero de sistemas palestino. Los aviones que surcan los cielos de Ciudad de México y los truenos que acompañas las lluvias veraniegas retrotraen su cuerpo a los bombardeos israelíes de 2025 en Gaza, en uno de los cuales murió su hija de cuatro años.
item.dc:creator: Diego Oré
item.content:encoded: Los ruidos fuertes aún le generan ansiedad a Mohammed Abed, un ingeniero de sistemas palestino. Los aviones que surcan los cielos de Ciudad de México y los truenos que acompañas las lluvias veraniegas retrotraen su cuerpo a los bombardeos israelíes de 2025 en Gaza, en uno de los cuales murió su hija de cuatro años. En la primavera de 2025, Abed, de 36 años, llegó a México junto con 17 familiares que buscaban asilo. Hoy en día, los martes por la mañana no comienzan con el temor a los bombardeos, sino con el trabajo. Antes del amanecer, carga su triciclo motorizado con comida palestina para venderla en un mercado al aire libre en Condesa, uno de los barrios más cosmopolitas de la capital. Abed es uno de los aproximadamente 160 palestinos que viven actualmente en México y parte de los casi 1.9 millones de palestinos desplazadas de sus hogares desde que comenzó la guerra en Gaza en 2023. La mayoría de quienes han abandonado el territorio se han reasentado en los países vecinos de Egipto y Jordania. Pero un puñado ha llegado a México, contribuyendo a que la población palestina del país se haya duplicado aproximadamente desde 2022, según cifras oficiales. "En Gaza, durante la guerra, escuchar un avión significaba que podía pasar algo terrible en cualquier momento", dijo durante un respiro de una extenuante jornada vendiendo hummus, baba ganush, falafel, shawarma y kebab. "El sonido me hace recordar todo lo que vivimos y mi cuerpo reacciona antes de que pueda pensar", agregó. El camino de Abed hacia México fue tortuoso. Comenzó con su padre, Kamal Abed, un palestino que emigró a México hace más de una década para escapar del conflicto en Gaza y que finalmente obtuvo la ciudadanía mexicana. Tras el estallido de la guerra en Gaza, en octubre de 2023, Kamal emprendió una campaña para sacar a su familia del enclave. En 2024, él viajó a Egipto para intentar organizar su evacuación, pero falleció de un infarto antes de poder completar el proceso. Otro hijo, Shadi, continuó con la labor y, con el apoyo de organizaciones civiles y abogados mexicanos, consiguió la autorización de viaje para 18 miembros de la familia, incluyendo varios niños. Después de meses de trámites y negociaciones para salir de Gaza, la familia cruzó a Jordania, pasó por Turquía y finalmente llegó a Ciudad de México en mayo de 2025, donde todos obtuvieron la residencia permanente. "No quiero política. Quiero vivir, como todos los demás, en paz", dijo Abed. "No queremos guerras; traen demasiadas muertes", agregó. Poco a poco, Abed se ha dado a conocer entre los clientes que disfrutan de sus platillos y se conmueven con su historia. Los domingos vende sus productos en otro mercado capitalino y, cuando no está allí, ayuda a su esposa a preparar los banquetes de comida palestina que ella ofrece para ocasiones especiales. La venta de comida les ayuda a reconstruir sus vidas después de perder su estatus durante la guerra. El hermano menor de Abed, Fadi, también vende comida palestina en Ciudad de México. Con su personalidad exuberante, este joven de 29 años ha logrado una base de 48,000 seguidores en Instagram bajo el usuario "hijo de Palestina", donde publica videos de su creciente negocio de comida en un español incipiente. Fadi, quien vendía frutos secos en Gaza, ahora quiere ahorrar lo suficiente para traer a sus dos hermanas a México y, con el tiempo, abrir un restaurante propio. La familia de Abed sigue creciendo. En mayo, su hijo menor, Yusuf, nació en la Ciudad de México, convirtiéndose automáticamente en ciudadano mexicano. "Nació en México, pero lleva en su corazón las raíces de Gaza", dijo, henchido de orgullo, Abed.

item.title: Oro cotiza estable antes de dato laboral en EEUU, en camino a caída semanal
item.description: Los precios del oro cotizaban estables el viernes, en camino de su segunda caída semanal consecutiva, ya que la fortaleza del dólar y el aumento del rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro lastraban el precio del lingote antes de la publicación de unos esperados datos sobre empleo en Estados Unidos.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Sinha
item.content:encoded: Los precios del oro cotizaban estables el viernes, en camino de su segunda caída semanal consecutiva, ya que la fortaleza del dólar y el aumento del rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro lastraban el precio del lingote antes de la publicación de unos esperados datos sobre empleo en Estados Unidos. * A las 0833 GMT, el oro al contado operaba plano a 4.181,59 dólares por onza, con un declive superior al 2% acumulado en lo que va de semana. Los futuros del oro en Estados Unidos subían un 0,2%, a 4.212 dólares. * "El oro encuentra apoyo a la espera del informe de empleo, tras unos datos de inflación del PCE más moderados de lo esperado que redujeron las apuestas por una subida de tasas de interés por parte de la Reserva Federal", dijo Nikos Tzabouras, analista senior de mercados de Tradu.com, propiedad de Jefferies. * Datos publicados el miércoles mostraron que la inflación en Estados Unidos se aceleró menos de lo esperado en agosto. Según la herramienta FedWatch de CME, los operadores ven ahora sólo un 26% de probabilidades de un alza de tasas este mes, comparado con el 70% de más temprano en la semana. * Las autoridades monetarias de la Fed se muestran muy divididas respecto a la futura política monetaria: algunos defendieron la necesidad de recabar más datos antes de decidir sobre una nueva subida de las tasas, mientras que otros abogaron por otro aumento para volver a encauzar la inflación. * El informe de empleo de septiembre en Estados Unidos se publicará a las 1230 GMT. Es probable que las nóminas no agrícolas hayan aumentado en 90.000 puestos el mes pasado, tras registrar un crecimiento de 162.000 en agosto, según un sondeo de Reuters a economistas. * El dólar se encamina a una subida semanal, mientras que el rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro a 10 y 30 años alcanzó el jueves sus niveles más altos desde 2002. * En otros metales preciosos, la plata al contado ganaba un 0,6%, a 61,21 dólares; el platino mejoraba un 0,7%, a 1.735,9 dólares; y el paladio avanzaba un 1,7%, a 1.191,2 dólares. Los tres metales se aprestan a cerrar la semana a la baja.

item.title: Russia will consider partial lifting of diesel export ban in case of overproduction, Novak says
item.description: Russia said on Friday it would consider a partial lifting of diesel export restrictions in case of overproduction, raising the prospect of a possible reprieve for global fuel markets strained by war and supply shortages.
item.dc:creator: Darya Korsunskaya
item.content:encoded: Russia said on Friday it would consider a partial lifting of diesel export restrictions in case of overproduction, raising the prospect of a possible reprieve for global fuel markets strained by war and supply shortages. Speaking in the upper chamber of the Russian parliament, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak also said that the domestic diesel market is currently balanced. Russia this week extended its ban on [USN:L8N45M0AV TEXT:"diesel exports"] for fuel producers until the end of October, adding further strain on the global energy market. Russia was the world's second-largest diesel exporter after the United States before it started to limit overseas sales this summer to meet the demand of the domestic market, supplies to which were dented by Ukrainian attacks on refineries. Global fuel shortages and sharp price increases have been in focus, especially in the United States, where diesel prices have shot to records over $6.50 a gallon as the wars in Iran and Ukraine constrain deliveries of fuel, a political risk for US President Donald Trump ahead of the midterm elections. "Today, the diesel market is balanced and supplies are sufficient. Although we extended the diesel export ban into October just a few days ago, we will continue to monitor the situation and, if diesel production exceeds domestic demand, we will consider partially reopening exports," Novak said. President Vladimir Putin said on Thursday that [USN:L8N45N1NG TEXT:"Russia will not supply its diesel"] to global energy markets until sanctions against Moscow are lifted. Novak said that the situation with Ukrainian drone attacks on Russia's energy infrastructure has remained "tense". He said Russia thwarted attacks on four refineries overnight, while the authorities were assessing the damage at one of the plants. Novak also said that the damage caused by repeated raids on refineries has been significantly lower thanks to protection measures. "This allows us to restore damaged equipment and bring facilities back into operation more quickly after repairs," he said.

item.title: Global equity funds draw inflows for second week as AI optimism holds
item.description: Global equity funds attracted inflows for a second straight week, as optimism around AI investment and softer US inflation pushed up investor demand for stocks despite rising bond yields.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Global equity funds attracted inflows for a second straight week, as optimism around AI investment and softer US inflation pushed up investor demand for stocks despite rising bond yields. Equity funds recorded net inflows of $34.76 billion in the week through September 30, down from $44.31 billion in the previous week, according to LSEG Lipper data. Risk appetite was largely supported by optimism over AI spending. Micron Technology (MU.O) on Wednesday [USN:L6N45M1AE TEXT:"forecast"] quarterly revenue above estimates, signaling strong demand for memory chips used in AI applications. Goldman Sachs said that the largest US hyperscalers are on track to spend about $800 billion on capital expenditure in 2026, with consensus expecting spending to rise to $1.1 trillion in 2027. The bank said strong revenue backlogs and a supply-constrained environment were continuing to support investment, while cloud revenue growth among major providers had accelerated sharply this year. Meanwhile, a Commerce Department [USN:L1N45M0L0 TEXT:"report"] on Wednesday showed that US inflation rose less than expected in August, while July price pressures were more moderate than initially reported, reducing the urgency for the Federal Reserve to raise rates again in October. Investors made net purchases of $20.6 billion in US equity funds for a second consecutive week. European and Asian equity funds also recorded net inflows of $6.19 billion and $6.16 billion, respectively. Sectoral funds, however, posted net weekly outflows of $919.7 million as investors withdrew $2.63 billion from technology funds after a three-week buying streak. They bought $1.13 billion in financial funds and $468 million in utility funds. Global bond funds attracted $4.76 billion in inflows for a second consecutive week, though this was substantially lower than inflows of $9.24 billion in the previous week. Short-term and government bond funds still registered significant inflows of $5.43 billion and $4.13 billion, respectively, while high-yield bond funds saw outflows of $2.29 billion. Money market funds posted net outflows of $116.52 billion — the largest weekly withdrawal since April 15. Among commodity funds, gold and precious-metals funds saw net weekly purchases of $275.2 million, their smallest inflow in three weeks. Energy funds posted net weekly outflows of $559 million, following inflows of $89.3 million the previous week. In emerging markets, equity funds recorded outflows of $1.37 billion for a fourth straight week. Investors also withdrew a net $1.75 billion from bond funds, according to data covering 29,099 funds.

item.title: Record numbers going hungry in Yemen amid escalating conflict, WFP says
item.description: Hunger in Yemen is accelerating, with a record number of people unable to meet their food needs as conflict intensifies in the country, the World Food Programme said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Le Poidevin
item.content:encoded: Hunger in Yemen is accelerating, with a record number of people unable to meet their food needs as conflict intensifies in the country, the World Food Programme said on Friday. Yemen is experiencing the most serious escalation between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-aligned Houthi group since a UN-brokered truce largely halted cross-border attacks in 2022. The renewed conflict has already displaced tens of thousands of people and could reshape control in Yemen, with implications for Red Sea shipping lanes and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Within a few weeks, a record number of people in government-controlled areas of the country where the WFP can access are no longer able to meet their food needs, with three out of four of households skipping meals, according to Matthew Hollingworth, the WFP’s Assistant Executive Director for Programme Operations. The total population of government-held areas is estimated at around 10 million people. “The effect of this latest flare-up of insecurity on the food security situation threatens to be absolutely devastating,” Hollingworth told reporters in Geneva via video link from Rome.

item.title: London shares recover as bond sell-off eases, oil prices slip
item.description: The UK's FTSE 100 rebounded on Friday, as easing oil and bond yields helped allay inflation concerns after a global bonds sell-off dented risk appetite earlier this week.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The UK's FTSE 100 rebounded on Friday, as easing oil and bond yields helped allay inflation concerns after a global bonds sell-off dented risk appetite earlier this week. The blue-chip FTSE 100 index (.FTSE) rose 0.28% to 10,455.34 points by 1007 GMT, but was headed for its sharpest weekly decline since April. The midcap FTSE 250 (.FTMC) climbed 0.52% to 24,267.39 points. Oil prices , eased about 3% after a sharp rise a day earlier as reports about talks on additional diesel and crude stock releases eased concerns over tight global energy supplies Global shares rose as wild volatility in bond and currency markets eased ahead of key US jobs data, which could shape expectations for the Federal Reserve's next policy move Gilt yields dropped, with the benchmark 10-year gilt yield falling to 5.332% after climbing to its highest since 2007 in the previous session The retreat in yields helped push rate-sensitive homebuilders (.FTNMX402020) up 1.1% after a 5% drop a day earlier Still, banks continued to remain under pressure, with the index of UK lenders (.FTNMX301010) set for its biggest weekly drop since March Among stocks, IG Group (IGG.L) tumbled 22% after the online trading platform cut its 2026 revenue growth [USN:L6N45O0AT TEXT:"forecast"], citing weak market conditions that hurt client retention in its over-the-counter (OTC) derivatives business. Peers Plus 500 (PLUSP.L) and CMC Markets (CMCX.L) declined 4.7% and 8.8%, respectively BAE Systems (BAES.L) advanced about 1% after [USN:L6N45N0T1 TEXT:"reports"] that the company is among the potential bidders that are in the early stages of exploring an offer for Robin Radar Systems Pub chain J D Wetherspoon (JDW.L) climbed 6.9% after [USN:L6N45O0AD TEXT:"reporting"] stronger sales growth since July, aided by sunny weather, while warning of rising costs and closures

item.dc:creator: Reinhard Becker, Klaus Lauer
item.content:encoded: Teure Energie hat die Inflation im Euro-Raum im September stark angefacht und auf den höchsten Stand seit drei Jahren getrieben. Die Verbraucherpreise stiegen um 3,8 Prozent, nach 3,2 Prozent im August, wie das EU-Statistikamt am Freitag mitteilte. Von Reuters befragte Experten hatten nur mit einem Wert von 3,6 Prozent gerechnet. Für den überraschend kräftigen Preisschub sorgte insbesondere Energie, die sich gegenüber dem Vorjahresmonat um satte 18,8 Prozent verteuerte. Die Europäische Zentralbank (EZB) dürfte sich bis zum Jahresende mit einer weiteren Zinserhöhung gegen den vom Iran-Krieg befeuerten Inflationsauftrieb stemmen. "Eine Zinsanhebung im Dezember ist so gut wie in Stein gemeißelt", meint der Chefvolkswirt der Liechtensteiner VP Bank, Thomas Gitzel. Während hierzulande die Inflationsrate mit 3,3 Prozent sogar unter dem Durchschnitt der Euro-Zone liegt, ist sie in Spanien (5,0 Prozent) und Italien (4,1 Prozent) weit darüber. "Der Süden wird für die EZB zum Problemfall", meint Gitzel. Auf ihrer Oktober-Zinssitzung dürften die Währungshüter seiner Ansicht nach allerdings noch die Füße stillhalten. EZB-Chefin Christine Lagarde hat bereits klargestellt, dass die Zinsen "nicht im Gleichschritt" mit den Energiepreisen steigen würden. "DIES WIRD DER EZB NICHT GEFALLEN" "Der sich hinziehende Energiepreisschock bleibt der entscheidende Treiber", sagte Stephanie Schoenwald, Ökonomin bei KfW Research, zu dem jüngsten Inflationsschub. Kriegsbedingt ausgedünnte Verarbeitungskapazitäten verschärften die Knappheiten bei Raffinerieprodukten, insbesondere bei Diesel, zusätzlich. Sie verweist darauf, dass auch die hohen Gaspreise zunehmend bei den europäischen Verbrauchern ankommen: "Gemeinsam mit wieder anziehenden mittelfristigen Inflationserwartungen der Haushalte stärkt das die Argumente für einen weiteren EZB-Zinsschritt." Nach Einschätzung von Commerzbank-Chefvolkswirt Jörg Krämer mehren sich zudem die Anzeichen, dass die Unternehmen die höheren Energiepreise an ihre Kunden weitergeben. In den vergangenen drei Monaten seien die Verbraucherpreise ohne Energie und Nahrungsmittel auf Jahresrate hochgerechnet bereits um schätzungsweise drei Prozent gestiegen: "Dieses Verfestigen der Inflation wird der EZB nicht gefallen. Sie wird ihre Leitzinsen weiter anheben müssen." Die Euro-Hüter hatten bereits im Juni und September auf den Inflationsschub infolge des anhaltenden Iran-Krieges reagiert und den Leitzins auf aktuell 2,50 Prozent angehoben. Die EZB rechnet damit, dass die Gesamtinflation noch bis in die erste Jahreshälfte 2027 deutlich über ihrem Zielwert von 2,0 Prozent bleiben wird. Sie will vermeiden, dass der Ölpreisschock das Preisgefüge nachhaltig verändert: Denn die vom Iran-Krieg angeheizten hohen Energiekosten für Verbraucher und Unternehmen bergen die Gefahr, dass sich Löhne und Preise gegenseitig hochschaukeln. EZB-Direktorin Isabel [USN:L8N45M1KS TEXT:"Schnabel"] betonte jüngst, dass man nicht abwarten könne, bis diese Effekte tatsächlich einträten. Es gelte zu beurteilen, wie sich Schocks auf die zugrunde liegende Inflation übertrügen, und die Geldpolitik entsprechend auszurichten. Die Zentralbank achtet dabei insbesondere auf die sogenannte Kernrate, bei der die schwankungsanfälligen Preise für Energie und Nahrungsmittel ausgeklammert werden. Diese Rate stieg im September auf 2,5 Prozent, nach 2,4 Prozent im Vormonat.

item.title: Romania's newest wind farm may add solar, storage, as country faces energy crunch
item.description: Rezolv Energy plans to add battery storage to the Vifor wind farm it launched this week in Romania and could add solar generating capacity too, its CEO said, as the country faces a power supply crunch after the idling of its sole nuclear plant.
item.dc:creator: Luiza Ilie, Marek Strzelecki
item.content:encoded: Rezolv Energy plans to add battery storage to the Vifor wind farm it launched this week in Romania and could add solar generating capacity too, its CEO said, as the country faces a power supply crunch after the idling of its sole nuclear plant. Romania [USN:L8N44A0GC TEXT:"suspended"] its last working nuclear reactor over the summer due to [USN:L8N4490NK TEXT:"low water levels"] on the Danube river, knocking out a fifth of the country's power capacity. It declared a state of energy emergency throughout August, asking consumers to cut power use during peak hours. [USN:L8N43H0IH TEXT:"Rezolv"], backed by British investor Actis, formally launched the 192 MW first phase of Vifor in Buzau County on Thursday after construction was completed, with the plant now feeding power into the grid. It now plans to add another source of power generation and storage capacity, potentially combining wind, solar panels, and batteries — so-called "hybridisation" — to create more stable supply, CEO Alastair Hammond told Reuters. "We already have the first step of planning to put a large battery there so that we can hybridize this wind farm," Hammond said. "We're also thinking potentially of completely hybridizing and actually putting solar panels in the region as well. So we'll have solar, wind, and storage." WIND FARM SLATED TO BE EUROPEAN UNION'S THIRD LARGEST The farm launches as solar output fades into autumn, while Romania's two nuclear reactors remain offline and hydropower production is low amid persistent drought. At the launch, wind whistled around the Vestas turbines — each of which can power about 1,000 homes — kicking up dust and blowing off hats. At full capacity in mid-2027, Vifor's 461 megawatts will make it the European Union's third-largest wind farm. Romania has added more than 1.5 gigawatts of renewable generation and 1 GW of storage so far this year. "The country still needs more storage and flexible capacity to keep the supply secure," said Alina Arsani of the Energy Policy Group think tank. With storage capacity insufficient to smooth intermittent output, imports help to keep the system balanced, the power grid operator said. "We can bring in energy at times when not enough power is produced in Romania," said Stefanita Munteanu, head of grid operator Transelectrica (ROTEL.BX) . "There is indeed additional pressure on interconnecting lines, but here we are two months after the reactors were shut down and the lights are still on."

item.title: Kongo: Mehr als 4000 Ebola-Tote
item.description: In der Demokratischen Republik Kongo sind nach Regierungsangaben inzwischen mehr als 4000 Menschen an Ebola gestorben. Zudem gebe es mittlerweile 8300 bestätigte Infektionsfälle in sieben Provinzen, teilte die Regierung am Freitag mit. Mehr als 2000 Patienten seien bislang genesen.
